edge: Use an empty anonymous program body.
negative: Put a net declaration directly inside an anonymous program.
positive: Put a task and class declaration in an anonymous program inside a package.

edge: Follow the import with only a parameter-port list.
negative: End an ANSI header immediately after a package import.
positive: Follow an ANSI-header import with a typed port declaration list.

edge: Export the same original declaration once explicitly and once through wildcard export.
positive: Export P::X twice in one package.

edge: Try to export X using a different package name from its import source.
negative: Export P::X when X is not an import candidate.
positive: Wildcard-import P, then explicitly export P::X to activate and re-export X.

edge: Explicitly import identically named identifiers from two different packages.
negative: Declare X locally and explicitly import P::X into the same scope.
positive: Explicitly import a name not otherwise declared or explicitly imported in the scope.

edge: Explicitly import one enumeration literal by name and use that literal unqualified.
positive: Explicitly import P::T and use T unqualified in the importing scope.

edge: Use package qualification for a literal when only its enum type was imported.
negative: Import only an enum type and use one of its literals unqualified.
positive: Import both an enum type and one of its literals explicitly, then use both unqualified.

edge: Export and import the name in adjacent declarations.
positive: Export P::X before a later wildcard import of P in the same package.

edge: Contrast two paths to one declaration with distinct declarations having the same name.
positive: Re-export one original declaration through two packages and import both paths.

edge: Use the imported name in a parameter declaration.
negative: Try to use the header-imported name in a separate design unit.
positive: Use a header-imported type in both a port and the design-unit body.

edge: Place multiple package imports before a parameter-port list.
negative: Place a package import after the header's port list.
positive: Place import P::* after a module identifier and before its port list.

edge: Access the declaration through its original package-qualified name from another scope.
negative: Hierarchically reference an imported-only name through the importing scope from outside.
positive: Use an imported identifier unqualified within its importing scope.

edge: Access the original P::X by qualification.
negative: Import P::X into Q without export, then expect Q import to expose X.
positive: Export an imported name and import it through the exporting package.

edge: Declare the same name in a nested scope.
negative: Activate wildcard-imported X, then declare or explicitly import X in the same scope.
positive: Declare a local name before any reference activates an identically named wildcard symbol.

edge: Compare a forward function call with a forward variable reference.
negative: Use a non-call identifier before its later declaration when no other rule makes it visible.
positive: Call a function declared later in the same scope.

edge: Reference the name of a nested scope from its containing scope.
negative: Reference a later local declaration before its declaration absent another visibility rule.
positive: Reference a local declaration after its declaration and an explicitly imported name after its import.

edge: Use a variable declaration with initialization, distinct from a net's implicit continuous assignment.
negative: Declare and initialize a package net in one net declaration.
positive: Declare an uninitialized net in a package.

edge: Use a package-qualified name directly in a class without an import statement.
negative: Place an import declaration directly among class members.
positive: Import P::T in an enclosing scope and use T within a nested class.

edge: Resolve a name available only from a compilation-unit-scope import.
positive: Reference in a nested block an unshadowed name wildcard-imported in its enclosing module.

edge: Place the package and importing module in one compilation input with the package first.
negative: Place an importing scope before the imported package in a controlled compilation order.
notes: Materialization must control compilation-unit and input order rather than depend on unspecified build-system ordering.
positive: Compile a package before a module that imports it.

edge: Declare an empty package with no optional closing identifier.
negative: Omit the semicolon after the package identifier.
positive: Declare a package containing a data declaration and a matching endpackage identifier.

edge: Use `export *::*;`.
negative: Use export without a package import item or global wildcard form.
positive: After importing P::X and Q::Y, export P::X, Q::Y in one declaration.

edge: Reference an identifier imported into the package from another package.
negative: Use a hierarchical path from a package item to an identifier in a module instance.
positive: Reference another declaration in the same package from a package function.

edge: Use a single explicit import item.
negative: Use an import item without a package identifier or scope-resolution operator.
positive: Import one named item and a wildcard item in a comma-separated declaration.

edge: Use the empty package_or_generate_item_declaration alternative represented by a semicolon.
negative: Place a module declaration directly as a package item.
positive: Place a typedef, function, checker, or class declaration in a package.

edge: Import an item from another package rather than relying on compilation-unit scope.
negative: Reference a compilation-unit variable from a package function.
positive: Use an item declared locally in the package.

edge: Declare process-free tasks and functions directly in a package.
negative: Place an initial or always process directly in a package.
positive: Declare a checker containing a procedural block inside a package.

edge: Use qualified references without importing the package's names.
negative: Qualify a name with a package that does not declare it.
positive: Declare a variable whose type is selected as P::T and initialize it with P::f().

edge: Observe several independently declaration-initialized package variables when an initial procedure starts.
notes: Use a runtime observation that does not depend on ordering among separate variable initializers.
positive: Observe a package variable's declaration-assigned value from an initial block at time zero.

edge: Use global wildcard export after actual imports from two packages.
negative: Expect an unactivated P wildcard candidate to be re-exported by P::*.
positive: Activate one wildcard candidate from P and export P::*, then import it downstream.

edge: Put the wildcard import in a different scope from the unqualified reference.
negative: Reference a package-declared identifier before the wildcard import.
positive: Wildcard-import a package before an unqualified reference to one of its declarations.

edge: Repeat the same import before and after unrelated declarations.
positive: Repeat `import P::X;` in the same scope.

edge: Provide the package's initial timeunits declaration in its dedicated pre-item position.
negative: Repeat a package timeunits declaration with a different unit or precision.
positive: Repeat the same timeunit/timeprecision declaration later in a package.

edge: Define a user identifier with the same name and resolve the user declaration unqualified.
positive: Use a declaration from std unqualified without an explicit import.

edge: Use the built-in declaration without std:: when no user declaration shadows it.
negative: Use an unknown name after std::.
positive: Use std:: qualification for a built-in type or function despite a colliding user name.

edge: Declare a colliding user function and use std:: qualification to select the built-in one.
positive: Call an unshadowed std function whose identifier has no dollar prefix.

edge: Provide a lexical function of the same name and verify it is selected before upward search.
positive: Call a task resolved by upward hierarchical search after lexical search has no match.

edge: Reference a wildcard-imported name available in the outermost lexical scope.
negative: Reference an undeclared variable name.
positive: Reference a declared local variable.

edge: Declare a local name matching a std name without modifying std.
negative: Attempt to reopen or otherwise add a declaration to std.
positive: Declare user names in a separate package.

edge: Import colliding names but never reference the ambiguous name.
negative: Wildcard-import two packages that both declare X and reference unqualified X.
positive: Wildcard-import two packages with distinct names and reference each.

edge: Declare a local identifier with the same name as one in a wildcard-imported package and resolve the local name.
positive: Wildcard-import P and use an otherwise undefined P identifier.

edge: Place the reference before versus after the wildcard import.
positive: Wildcard-import P, then reference X where P declares X and no local X exists.
